gaps.gap_id: C1 — Safe modules and guard never probed
gaps.real: PARTLY — the code gap is real, the *quoted evidence for its harmlessness is FALSE*. Code gap verified: `_CLASSIFY_PROBE_SIGS` is at services/resolution/tracking.py:556-563 and fires exactly 6 zero-argument selectors (getOwners/getThreshold/getMinDelay/delay/UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION/owner); `_get_storage_at` is at tracking.py:463-469. `grep -rn '4a204f620c8c5ccdca3fd54d003badd85ba500436a431f0cbda4f558c93c34c8|cc2f8452|guard_manager|getModulesPaginated|isModuleEnabled' --include=*.py --include=*.js --include=*.json .` → ZERO hits anywhere in the repo. REFUTATION of B0b/R1's closing caveat and FIELDS.md:84: B0b says 'probed on all 9 Safes at 25643300, getModulesPaginated returns [] with the sentinel and the guard slot is zero, so k/n is currently exact'. The Safe-principal population is 19, not 9 (`select count(distinct lower(address)) from function_principals where resolved_type='safe'` → 19; control_graph_nodes → 18; principal_labels → 20; protocol-1-scoped → 11; monitored_contracts contract_type='safe' → 11 — NO plane yields 9). I probed all 19 at pinned block 25643300 via utils/rpc: 18 return modules=[] with next=0x…01, and **0x21f73d42eb58ba49ddb685dc29d3bf5c0f0373ca (Safe VERSION() '1.1.1', threshold 4, 9 owners) returns modules=['0x2e1b5a40edc922bce489668b11749b8eabd67f6b'] — one ENABLED MODULE** (Etherscan: ContractName 'ConfirmedTransactionModule', VERSION() '0.1.0', 5,452 bytes of code). Guard slot 0x4a204f62… reads zero on 19/19; module-guard slot 0xb104e0b9… zero on 19/19. So on this corpus k/n is an upper bound on protection for 1 of 19 Safe principals, and the register published the opposite as a corpus-level positive fact from a 9-row subset — the exact absence-as-proof error. Independent cross-witness (19/19 byte-agreement): eth_getStorageAt at `modules[SENTINEL_MODULES]` = keccak256(abi.encode(address(0x1), uint256(1))) = 0xcc69885fda6bcc1a4ace058b4a62bf5e179ea78fd58a1ccd71c22cc9b688792f returns 0x…01 on the 18 and exactly 0x…2e1b5a40edc922bce489668b11749b8eabd67f6b on 0x21f73d42. Monitor half: ZERO cursors on any Safe address (`select count(*) from indexed_event_cursors where lower(event_address) in (safe set)` → 0 of 80 cursors); EnabledModule/DisabledModule/ChangedGuard/AddedOwner/RemovedOwner/ChangedThreshold/Upgraded/CallExecuted/ExecutionSuccess are ALL unenrolled (0 of the 25 enrolled topic0s). services/monitoring/event_topics.py:73-89 already maps ExecutionFromModuleSuccess/Failure → safe_module_executed/safe_module_failed, i.e. the pipeline can see a module EXECUTE but not a module being ENABLED.

gaps.provable: PROVABLE via on-chain read (pinned block) — TWO independent deterministic witnesses that agree 19/19, plus a compiler/source-derived preimage check. The guard slot preimage was verified against DEPLOYED source, not memory: Etherscan getsourcecode on the actual singletons read from slot 0 of each Safe — 0x41675c099f32341bf84bfc5382af534df5c7461a (Safe 1.4.1) and 0xd9db270c1b5e3bd161e8c8503c55ceabee709552 (GnosisSafe 1.3.0) both contain the literal constant `GUARD_STORAGE_SLOT = 0x4a204f620c8c5ccdca3fd54d003badd85ba500436a431f0cbda4f558c93c34c8` with the comment naming the preimage `guard_manager.guard.address`, which I recomputed as keccak256('guard_manager.guard.address') = the same 32 bytes. THREE-STATE CAVEAT that must be published, not collapsed: the third singleton 0x34cfac646f301356faa8b21e94227e3583fe3f5f (GnosisSafe 1.1.1 — the module-bearing Safe) contains NO guard feature at all (no GUARD_STORAGE_SLOT, no ChangedGuard event in its source). A zero read at that slot on a 1.1.1 Safe is 'feature absent', NOT 'guard disabled', and reading it as the latter would be a defaulted witness. Likewise `module_manager.module_guard.address` exists only from Safe 1.5.0; zero on all 19 is 'feature absent'. So the publication is: guard ∈ {proven_address, proven_zero (1.3.0/1.4.1 only), feature_absent (1.1.1), not_determined (read failed)}. The monitor half is PROVABLE as an event fold ONLY under B0b/R9's fourth limit: EnabledModule/DisabledModule/ChangedGuard have non-indexed args in 1.1.1/1.3.0 and indexed in 1.4.1 (verified in the three deployed sources), so the same topic0 carries the module address in DATA on some versions and TOPICS on others — a folder that reads only topics silently mints an empty module set on 1.3.0.
gaps.proposed_witness: Per Safe principal, at a recorded block: {`modules`: the getModulesPaginated array cross-checked against the `modules[SENTINEL]` storage word, or `not_determined` on read failure; `guard`: one of proven_address / proven_zero / feature_absent(<version>) / not_determined; `safe_version`: the VERSION() string; `singleton`: slot-0 word; `probe_block`: the integer height}. Then `protection_exact: true` may be published ONLY when modules is a proven empty AND guard is proven_zero-or-feature_absent AND the version is known; otherwise `protection_is_upper_bound: true` with the module list cited. Nothing may be inferred from a *missing* modules key.

gaps.gap_id: C3 — ManagerWithMerkleVerification absent from contracts (10 addresses)
gaps.real: YES, exactly 10, and the 'sole canCall' claim holds 10/10. `select fp.address, count(*), count(distinct ef.contract_id), exists(contracts row), exists(job) from function_principals fp join effective_functions ef on ef.id=fp.function_id where ef.function_name='manage' group by 1` → **10 distinct addresses, 2 rows each (the two `manage` overloads), 1 contract each, 0 present in `contracts`, 0 with a job**. Per-vault: `select ef.contract_id, count(distinct fp.address) ... where ef.function_name='manage' group by 1` → 10 vaults (contract_ids 22, 47, 76, 80, 81, 82, 83, 84, 91, 95 — BoringGovernance 0x86b5780b + 9 BoringVaults), each with exactly **1 distinct principal**, origin `semantic_capability:finite_set`, resolved_type 'contract'. On-chain at pinned 25643300, all 10 managers: `vault()` returns EXACTLY the BoringVault whose `manage` they gate — 10/10 structural back-link, no exceptions; code sizes cluster into two bytecode variants (7,921 and 8,348 bytes); each has its own distinct `authority()`. Etherscan ContractName on the sampled ones: ManagerWithMerkleVerification. Presence audit: `in contract_dependencies` 0/10, `in controller_values` 0/10, `in monitored_contracts` 0/10, but **`in control_graph_nodes` 10/10** with node_type='contract', resolved_type='contract', analysis_state='analyzed', analyzed=true, depth=1, label='ManagerWithMerkleVerification'. CORRECTION to the register: B10.5 credits these with 'the M10-confirmed 60 contract-gated warnings'. Measured: `contract_gated_unknown_path` totals 68 / 60 / 64 in score.json / score_v2.json / score_v3.json, of which **exactly 30 are manager-attributable in all three**. 60 was the whole warning class, not the managers' share.
gaps.fixable: YES, and unlike C2 this one IS a structural bug with a one-call fix. The 10 manager nodes carry `details = {"source": "semantic_capability:role_grant", "address": …}` — the marker minted at services/policy/capability_surface.py:236, i.e. they are added by the POLICY stage's role-principal projection. `workers/policy_worker.py:686-712` reassigns the refreshed graph, calls `store_artifact(…, 'resolved_control_graph', data=refreshed_graph)` and `replace_control_graph_rows(...)` — but **never calls `_queue_discovered_contracts`**. The only call site is `workers/resolution_worker.py:286`, which runs earlier in the pipeline. So every node first discovered by the policy refresh is permanently outside the analysis perimeter, even though it satisfies every gate in the spawn loop (resolution_worker.py:568-573: analyzed truthy, node_type=='contract'). Blast radius measured: `select details->>'source', node_type, count(distinct address), count(distinct address) filter (no job) from control_graph_nodes group by 1,2` → `semantic_capability:role_grant` / contract: **32 addresses, 19 with no job** (the 10 managers plus 9 others); role_grant/principal: 7 addresses, 7 with no job. Fix: invoke the same `_queue_discovered_contracts` after the policy-stage `replace_control_graph_rows` (policy_worker.py:712), or emit the newly-discovered addresses onto `monitoring_enrollment_queue`-style follow-up work. The fact is fully in scope there: `refreshed_graph`, `job`, `session`, `rpc_url` are all live locals.
gaps.provable: PROVABLE, and by two independent instruments. (1) On-chain read (pinned block): `vault()` on each manager returns the gated BoringVault, 10/10 at 25643300 — a deterministic structural identity that needs no name. (2) Stored provenance, not inference: the reason these are outside the perimeter is read off `control_graph_nodes.details->>'source' = 'semantic_capability:role_grant'`, a persisted field written by a named code path, joined against `jobs` — no name-matching, no default, no absence. Note explicitly what is NOT provable and is NOT being claimed: I am not inferring the contract's role from the string 'ManagerWithMerkleVerification' in `control_graph_nodes.label` (that label is name-derived and is exactly the T-LABELS trap). The load-bearing facts are the `vault()` back-link and the finite-set membership fold, both witnesses. This is an inv.8 discovery-perimeter fix, not a scoring fix: no scorer change makes an unanalysed contract's authority walkable.
gaps.proposed_witness: One completed analysis job per manager address, producing its own `effective_functions` + `function_principals`, so the Boring `manage` gate resolves to keys instead of terminating at a contract. Until then the correct publication is what the scorer already emits — `contract_gated_unknown_path` with `missing_witness: 'controlling principal of the gating contract'` — plus, newly available at zero RPC cost, the proven `vault()` back-link and the manager's own `authority()` address as a cited but unresolved next hop.
gaps.honest_publication: n/a for the perimeter fix (provable). One thing must stay three-state even after the fix: the manager's merkle root (`manageRoot(strategist)`) bounds what `manage` can do, and a root hash is not a decodable permission set — the strategist's admissible calls are `not_determined` from on-chain state alone. Do not let 'the manager is analysed' become 'the manage capability is bounded'.

gaps.real: YES on every quoted number, and the schema claim is absolute. `\d upgrade_events` → columns are exactly (id, contract_id, proxy_address, old_impl, new_impl, block_number, timestamp, tx_hash, source); `select table_name, column_name from information_schema.columns where column_name ilike any('%sender%','%tx_from%','%from_addr%','%executor%','%caller%','%initiator%')` → **0 rows in the entire schema**. Protocol-1 slice: `select count(*), count(distinct tx_hash), count(distinct lower(proxy_address)) from upgrade_events ue join contracts c on c.id=ue.contract_id where c.protocol_id=1` → **120 events / 68 distinct tx_hash / 24 proxies**, source='backfill' on all, old_impl NULL on all (191 rows table-wide, not the ledger's 189 — L-120(b) is stale by 2). Max fanout confirmed: tx 0xc9c80e5bc8a3f2eedfca80030eba7a5531bcb23774ca9da3e29a591032570314 carries **19 events across 19 proxies** at block 25533308 / 2026-07-14 20:36:23Z, so per-event attribution would indeed 19× one governance action. I then pulled all 68 receipts and folded the logs against keccak-matched topic0s. The 68 partition COMPLETELY and with no residue (18+23+15+4+8 = 68 txs; 18+67+23+4+8 = 120 events): **18 txs / 18 events are proxy DEPLOYMENTS** (receipt.to is null; verified 6/6 sampled that receipt.contractAddress == the proxy_address in the row, e.g. 0x0c9b77a5fe→0x8f08b704…, 0x491b823bc1→0x308861a4…); **23 txs / 67 events** carry TimelockController `CallExecuted` + Safe `ExecutionSuccess` (timelock-routed); **15 txs / 23 events** carry `ExecutionSuccess` with NO `CallExecuted` (Safe upgraded directly); **4 txs / 4 events** carry neither marker with receipt.to == the proxy itself (one-hop EOA); **8 txs / 8 events** carry neither marker with receipt.to == a small intermediary (0x356d1b83970cef2018f2c9337cddb67dff5aef99, 6 txs, 1,164 bytes of code; 0xdbf6be120d4dc72f01534673a1223182d9f6261d, 2 txs, 1,064 bytes). Consequence the register does not state: **18 of 120 stored 'upgrades' are deployments** — EtherFiNodesManager 0x8b71140a is 18 stored / **17 real**, LiquidityPool 0x308861a4 is 17 stored / **16 real**, and 0x2b90103c has 1 stored / **0 real**; 18 of 24 proxies carry exactly one such phantom.
gaps.fixable: PARTLY, and only in one direction. Write site is `services/discovery/upgrade_history.py:592-606` — the `UpgradeEvent(...)` constructor, which has no executor column and no receipt in scope. Parse site `parse_upgrade_log` at :114-140 receives a single Etherscan log dict: `transactionHash`, `blockNumber`, `timeStamp`, `topics`, `address` — **the executor fact is NOT in scope there**, so no amount of care at the parse site can produce it. Making it available costs one `eth_getTransactionReceipt` per DISTINCT tx_hash (68 for protocol 1, 107 for the whole table), joined by tx_hash at the projection site. `indexed_event_logs` carries tx_hash and could support the identical fold with zero receipt reads — but it stores no `to`/`from`, and none of Upgraded / CallExecuted / ExecutionSuccess is enrolled (0 of the 25 enrolled topic0s; 0 cursors on any Safe address), so that route needs an unbounded genesis-to-head backfill and would still not distinguish one-hop-EOA from mediated. The receipt read is the cheaper and STRONGER instrument here, because a receipt's log set is complete-for-that-transaction by construction, which is exactly the coverage property B0b/R9's fourth limit demands and a cursor plane cannot cheaply give.
gaps.provable: SPLIT — and this is the load-bearing answer. (a) 'Which EOA authorised it' is **NOT PROVABLE**: tx.from on a Safe execTransaction is a relayer, and I measured the relayer confound directly — 11 of the 15 Safe-direct txs were relayed to Safe 0xf155a2632ef263a6a382028b3b33feb29175b8a5 by SIX different `from` addresses (0x46cba1e9…, 0xfa238cb3…, 0x5dfb8bc4…, 0xfe27543a…, 0x71b67ac9…), so tx.from names the submitter, never the signer set. Publish `authorising_eoa: not_determined` — always. (b) 'Which contract EXECUTED it' IS **PROVABLE via an event fold over the transaction's own receipt** — a keccak-selector/topic match plus a completeness property that holds by construction. The verdict is four-valued and each value is a positive fact: `timelock_routed` (a CallExecuted from an address independently classified as a timelock), `safe_direct` (an ExecutionSuccess from a classified Safe with no CallExecuted anywhere in the tx), `eoa_one_hop` (no executor marker AND receipt.to == the proxy — here and ONLY here tx.from is the msg.sender at the proxy, so it is the authoriser as a matter of EVM semantics, not inference), and `deployment` (receipt.to is null AND receipt.contractAddress == the proxy). (c) The 8 mediated txs are **NOT PROVABLE from the receipt** and must publish `executor: not_determined` — the intermediary could be an unmodelled Safe, a factory, or a custom governance shim; I read only its code size. (d) THE DECOY TEST, and its honest answer. inv.5's rule needs an EXISTENCE proof that a principal can upgrade without the delay. The fold constructs exactly that shape, and on this corpus it comes out NEGATIVE: 8 proxies have both a timelock-routed and a Safe-direct upgrade, and for every one of them the count of Safe-direct upgrades occurring AFTER that proxy's first timelock-routed upgrade is **0** (first_timelock blocks 19507905 / 19507905 / 20916930 / 20916930 / 21666732 / 22131382 / 25533308 / 25533308; zero later direct upgrades on all 8). Every direct-Safe upgrade predates the timelock era. So the fold proves 'a direct path was exercised at block B', and proves NOTHING about whether it is open now — 'the timelock is not a decoy' would be absence-as-proof and must not be published.
gaps.proposed_witness: Per distinct tx_hash: {`executor_kind` ∈ {timelock_routed, safe_direct, eoa_one_hop, deployment, not_determined}, `executor_address` (the CallExecuted / ExecutionSuccess emitter, or receipt.to for eoa_one_hop, else null), `authorising_eoa`: always `not_determined`, `receipt_read_at_block`: receipt.blockNumber, `is_deployment`: bool with basis receipt.contractAddress == proxy_address, `governance_action_id`: the tx_hash itself}. The last field is the fix for the 19× double-count: aggregate on tx_hash, never on event id. And an explicitly separate, non-derivable field: `direct_path_currently_open`: `not_determined` unless a current-state authority read says otherwise.
gaps.honest_publication: Three statements must ship as `not_determined`, stated plainly: (1) `authorising_eoa` on all 38 Safe-mediated and timelock-routed txs — tx.from is a relayer, measured 6 relayers for 1 Safe. (2) `executor_kind` on the 8 intermediary-mediated txs. (3) `timelock_is_decoy` on all 24 proxies — the fold's 0-after-first-timelock result is an ABSENCE of observed bypass, not proof that no bypass exists; the only thing publishable from history is the positive `direct_upgrade_witnessed_at_block: <B>` on the 15 Safe-direct txs, which for all 8 dual-class proxies carries a block PRIOR to the timelock's first use and therefore licenses no current claim either way.
gaps.deterministic_test: tests/test_upgrade_executor_fold.py, PR#161 style with pinned receipt fixtures (stub the wire, no network). Use the real measured transactions as fixtures so the expectations are byte-exact: (1) 0xc9c80e5bc8a3f2eedfca80030eba7a5531bcb23774ca9da3e29a591032570314 ⇒ executor_kind 'timelock_routed', 19 events collapsing to ONE governance_action_id, and an explicit assertion that the aggregate counts 1 action not 19. (2) 0x142d4eb943… (ExecutionSuccess from 0xf46d3734564ef9a5a16fc3b1216831a28f78e2b5, no CallExecuted) ⇒ 'safe_direct' with executor_address == that Safe and authorising_eoa == 'not_determined' EVEN THOUGH receipt.from is populated — this is the test that pins the reject-list rule. (3) 0x91ead36d1f… (receipt.to null, contractAddress == 0xb49e4420…) ⇒ is_deployment True and the row EXCLUDED from any upgrade count; assert EtherFiNodesManager's published count is 17, not 18. (4) 0x3440c10946… (no markers, to == proxy 0xb49e4420…) ⇒ 'eoa_one_hop' with executor_address == receipt.from. (5) 0x884ad34345… (no markers, to == 0x356d1b83…, ≠ proxy) ⇒ 'not_determined', executor_address null — FAIL-CLOSED, and specifically assert it is NOT 'eoa_one_hop'. (6) FAIL-CLOSED: eth_getTransactionReceipt returns null ⇒ 'not_determined', and the row must not be dropped or defaulted to any kind. (7) FAIL-CLOSED: a receipt whose ExecutionSuccess emitter is an address NOT classified as a Safe ⇒ 'not_determined', not 'safe_direct' (blocks minting a Safe verdict from an unverified emitter — the 11 txs on the unmodelled 0xf155a263… Safe are exactly this case). (8) Decoy-rule pin: a fixture where a Safe-direct upgrade postdates the first timelock-routed one ⇒ `direct_upgrade_after_timelock: true`; the real 8-proxy data ⇒ `false` on all 8, with the published field being `not_determined` for `timelock_is_decoy` in BOTH arms of the false case. Plus a topic pin asserting keccak256('CallExecuted(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256,bytes)') == 0xc2617efa69bab66782fa219543714338489c4e9e178271560a91b82c3f612b58 and keccak256('Upgraded(address)') == 0xbc7cd75a20ee27fd9adebab32041f755214dbc6bffa90cc0225b39da2e5c2d3b.
gaps.cost: SCHEMA MIGRATION REQUIRED — this is the only Group C item that needs one. Either 3-4 new columns on `upgrade_events` (executor_kind, executor_address, is_deployment, receipt_read_at_block) or, cleaner given the 19× fanout, a new `upgrade_transactions` table keyed on (chain_id, tx_hash) with `upgrade_events` referencing it — which is also the only shape that fixes the double-count structurally. RPC: 68 eth_getTransactionReceipt for protocol 1, 107 for the whole table, ONE-TIME (a mined receipt is immutable, so it is cacheable forever); +1 per distinct tx on each future backfill. REWRITES EXISTING PERSISTED ROWS: yes — a backfill would stamp all 191 rows, and 18 of the 120 protocol-1 rows would be reclassified as deployments, changing every derived upgrade count. Note `project_to_events` at upgrade_history.py:562/581 already does a destructive delete+reinsert per contract, so the backfill has an existing (if unlovely) vehicle.
gaps.flips_existing_rows: Two sets. (1) NO row in scoring_prototype/score_v3.json flips — there is no upgrade-derived finding or warning today, so the executor fold changes no verdict and, per (d) above, does NOT retract any timelock credit (the anti-decoy answer is negative). (2) Published COUNTS in SCORING_INVARIANTS.md's B9 row (line 1566) flip: 'EtherFiNodesManager **18 upgrades** (2023-05-02 → 2026-07-14), LiquidityPool 17, Liquifier 8, EETH 6' becomes 17 / 16 / 7 / 5 once the deployment-time `Upgraded` events are excluded; the '**11 proxies upgraded on 2026-07-14**' figure is also wrong — the single tx 0xc9c80e5b… at block 25533308 that day touched **19** proxies. Total 'upgrade_events 120 rows / 24 proxies' becomes 102 real upgrades / 23 proxies with any real upgrade (0x2b90103cdc9bba6c0dbcaaf961f0b5b1920f19e3 drops to zero). B14 flags: 4 one-hop-EOA txs, 2 mediating intermediaries, 3 Safe-direct txs by 0xf46d3734 and 1 by 0xa000244b — all under 5, none may calibrate a rule.
